base_rate.description: Build cost per unit of building volume, before the tier and fit-out multipliers (§5.3).

ClassF64.description: A float per class (scoring inputs only).

base_rate.description: Land rent per unit of building volume per day, before the tier multiplier (§5.3, R10).

lease_term_years.description: Lease length in in-game years (§5.2, default 30).

lot_property_uplift.description: Share of every property's value credited to the lot's leaseholder (R39, default 0.2).

value_method.description:
How a held lease's land is valued for net worth (§3; docs/economy.md "Land value").
Default `book_decay`, the spec's `last auction price × years left / term`.

LandValueMethod.description:
How a held lease's land counts towards net worth (§3). The spec's formula is
`book_decay`; the others are balance-study candidates (docs/economy.md "Land value").

oneOf.description: `last auction price × remaining lease years / term` (§3, the default).

`current land base price × remaining lease years / term`: the block's price today
(moved by desirability shifts and land-value events such as the 2008 crash).
`current land base price` while the lease runs, nothing once it has run out.

sell_to_city_ratio.description: Instant sale back to the city, as a share of true value (R5, default 0.5).

starting_cash.description: Cash each player starts with (R62, default £7,000), on top of the overdraft.

interest_rate.description: Daily interest on overdrawn balances (default 0: R32 says none).

PopulationEconomy.description: How many people there are and how they spend (§8).

allowance_by_class.description:
Daily allowance per class before the age and sex multipliers (`customers.yaml`
`allowance`; §8.2, R55).

births_multiplier.description:
Multiplier on every era's births per woman (`customers.yaml` `births_per_woman`, the
historical table; R61). 1 = history.

migration_per_day.description: Migrants added to each morning's arrivals.

comfortable_share.description: Comfortable rent share of allowance (R52, default 0.2).

commute_preference.description:
Study lever, off by default (0): the share of the city's adults who would rather
commute than live in a flat, even one they can afford. The 05:30 house-hunt houses no
more than `⌊adults × (1 − commute_preference)⌋` (docs/economy.md "Residential levers").

default_rent.description: Rent per flat per day until the owner sets one: the city's default (R4, R51).

flat_size.description: Units of volume per flat (R50, default 4).

max_rent_per_flat.description:
Study lever, off by default (`null`): the most any flat's rent can be per day. An
owner may set more, but residents see and pay `min(rent, cap)` (docs/economy.md
"Residential levers").

move_interval_years.description: Minimum in-game years between moves (R54, default 10).

reference_rent.description: The reference rent for `price_factor` when people weigh flats (R51).

rent_tax.description:
Study lever, off by default (0): the share of residents' rent paid to the city as tax
at the 06:00 settlement; the owner gets the rest (docs/economy.md "Residential levers").

stretch_min_desirability.description:
A flat whose desirability (class affinity × fit-out appeal) is at least this justifies
stretching to `stretch_share` (R52).

stretch_share.description: Stretch rent share for desirable flats (R52, default 0.5).

base_rates.description: Bill per unit of building volume per day, before the business's utility factor (§5.3).

internet_base_rate.description:
The telephone exchange's base rate once it becomes the internet (R11; the year is
`utilities.yaml` `internet.upgrade_year`).

demand_multipliers.description:
A multiplier on what shoppers want, by decade (§8.2, R64): `"1930s": 1.0`. Each applies
from its decade's first year until the next decade named; the first must be at or before
the start of every game. `P(good)` is multiplied after the segment rules and capped at 1.

land.description: Land rent, leases and how land counts towards net worth (§3, §5).

money.description: Players' money: starting cash, the overdraft and selling up (§2.3, §3).

population.description: How many people there are and how they spend (§8).
